why: The em dash (U+2014) is banned in every text (D27).
fix: Use a full stop, a comma, a colon or brackets.

why: The en dash (U+2013) is banned in every text (D27); on a phone it looks like an em dash.
fix: Write ranges as "2 to 3" and joined names with a hyphen.

why: The horizontal bar (U+2015) is banned in every text (D27).
fix: Use a full stop, a comma, a colon or brackets.

why: A verb people rarely write and generated text often does.
fix: Say "look at", "study" or "read".

why: Claims smoothness instead of describing what happens.
fix: Say what happens, with a number if there is one.

why: A longer word for "use".
fix: Say "use".

why: Announces a fact instead of stating it.
fix: Delete the phrase and state the fact.

why: A stock opener that says nothing about the subject.
fix: Delete it and start with the subject.

why: A worn figure of speech in place of a concrete claim.
fix: Name the thing and what it does.

why: Marketing verbs that promise without saying how.
fix: Use a plain verb: "lets", "helps", "speeds up".

why: A rhetorical setup that delays the point.
fix: State the point plainly.

why: Tour-guide filler before the content.
fix: Delete it and give the content.

pattern: \b(?:as an ai\b|i hope this helps|great question|happy to help|feel free to)|\b(?:certainly|absolutely)!
why: Phrases left over from a chat reply.
fix: Delete them.

why: No emoji in docs, forms, issues, pull requests or commits; a screen reader reads each one aloud by name.
fix: Use words.

why: No exclamation marks in docs, forms, pull requests or commits.
fix: End with a full stop.

why: The game may celebrate a result, at most once per screen.
fix: Make it a statement, or mark the one celebration with copy-ok.

why: Issues and comments read better without exclamation marks.
fix: End with a full stop.

why: Vague praise; it does not say what the thing survives.
fix: Say what it handles: the input, the failure, the range.

why: An adjective that praises instead of measuring.
fix: Delete it, or replace it with a number.

why: A word that adds length and no meaning.
fix: Delete it and reread the sentence.

why: A connective that pads the start of a sentence.
fix: Delete it; the order of sentences already connects them.

why: A contrast set up to sound bigger than the claim.
fix: State the main claim directly.

why: A metaphor for a process; in this game a flight is a flight.
fix: Name the trip or the steps.

why: Addresses an imagined crowd instead of the reader.
fix: Name who the text is for.

why: Landscape as a figure of speech for a field or a market.
fix: Name the thing.

why: Navigate as a figure of speech; keep the word for real paths.
fix: Use a concrete verb: handle, choose, follow.

why: Unlock as a promise; unlocking a level stays fine.
fix: Say what becomes possible.

why: Markdown source uses ASCII quotes; curly quotes belong in UI strings only.
fix: Use ' and ".

why: A sentence over 35 words is hard to follow, and harder through a screen reader.
fix: Split it.

why: A list of three in a short sentence is often there for rhythm, not content.
fix: Check each item is real; use two, or four, when there are two or four.

why: Headings use sentence case.
fix: Capitalise the first word and proper nouns only.
